newsitem.title: USA: Burger King could hire thousands off welfare rolls.
newsitem.headline: Burger King could hire thousands off welfare rolls.

text.p: Burger King Corp., one of five major corporations to join President Clinton's national effort to move people from welfare to work, said Wednesday it could envision hiring up to 15,000 welfare recipients a year.
Vincent Berkeley, Burger King vice president of diversity and corporate affairs, said the company had no set target for welfare hiring.
But he said it was conceivable that 50 percent of Burger King's annual hiring of 20,000 to 30,000 nationwide could come from welfare rolls.

"The majority of our development, probably for the next several years, will be inner city-type development," Berkeley said. "I would give you what I would say is a conservative type estimation that over 50 percent potentially could come from the rolls."
Burger King and its franchisees employ about 300,000 people in the United States.

In his State of the Union message on Tuesday, President Clinton said Burger King, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, Sprint Corp., Monsanto Co., United Parcel Service, and UAL Corp.'s United Airlines would be the first to join in "a new national effort to marshal America's businesses, large and small, to create jobs so people on welfare can move to work."
Berkeley said the positions offered to welfare recipients largely would be entry-level jobs in restaurants -- cooks and cashiers -- but that those jobs had "high upward mobility potential."
Berkeley called the programme a "tremendous business opportunity" for Burger King in an industry where it is often difficult to recruit entry-level workers.

But he warned that the public-private partnership would not thrive without a successful public sector effort to solve the social issues of welfare recipients, including transportation and child care. (UAL.N GMET.L FON.N MTC.N)
